goals.0: Names of body parts and their articles
goals.1: „Mein Kopf tut weh“ — saying where it hurts
dialog.0.de.2.n: Was ist los? = What's wrong? (asked when something seems off)
dialog.1.de.2.n: wehtun: Mein Kopf tut weh — tut when the body part is singular
grammar.0.title: Body parts and their plurals
grammar.0.note: Bangla has a single word for “hand”, but German separates Arm (shoulder to wrist) from Hand (wrist to fingers). Foot and leg work the same way: Bein and Fuß.
grammar.1.title: wehtun — “it hurts”
grammar.1.text: „Mein Kopf tut weh.“ (My head hurts.) When the body part is plural, use tun: „Meine Augen tun weh.“, „Mein Rücken und mein Bauch tun weh.“ Separable verb: wehtun → tut … weh.
grammar.2.title: Compound words for pain — Ich habe …
grammar.2.intro: Join Schmerzen (pain) to the name of a body part. The word is always plural.
grammar.2.note: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen. = I have a headache. (no article.)
quiz.6.why: Two or more body parts (Augen) → tun.
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order: “My head hurts.”
